subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Where should the shared multi-encoding filename decoder live, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/71517 be refreshed or replaced?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent boundary affects core media helpers, bundled channel plugins, and plugin-facing reuse, so automation should not choose the API direction alone.

options.title: Use media-core or SDK-safe decoder
options.body: Move the decoder into media-core or an explicitly exported plugin-safe boundary, then refresh the candidate PR or replacement around that shared helper.

options.title: Keep narrow channel repairs only
options.body: Treat current Feishu fixes as sufficient for now and wait for concrete non-Feishu channel reports before approving a shared utility.

options.title: Require broader live repros first
options.body: Keep this issue open but ask for real non-Feishu channel failures before approving a shared decoder API.

recommendation.title: Use media-core or SDK-safe decoder
recommendation.body: Move the decoder into media-core or an explicitly exported plugin-safe boundary, then refresh the candidate PR or replacement around that shared helper.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Feishu filename fixes and media-core/release context make this the strongest available owner for the boundary decision.
